t:
Section 10751 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking out “(other than transportation by rail)” in subsections (a) and (b).
 
    (b) 
The provisions of section 10751 of title 49, United States Code, as amended by subsection (a) of this section, shall apply to any expense of the type described in subsection (a) of such section 10751 that was incurred prior to the effective date of this Act (other than an expense with respect to which a penalty was paid pursuant to section 10761 of such title 49) or that is incurred on or after such effective date.

fable.w: This section is a technical amendment striking a rail-transportation exclusion from 49 U.S.C. 10751 and setting the temporal scope of the amended provision for expenses incurred before or after the effective date. The only tempting reading is that references to a "penalty" or carrier expenses imply some process with outside parties, but no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is created. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: shall apply to any expense of the type described in subsection (a) of such section 10751 that was incurred prior to the effective date of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute regarding the scope of expenses covered by a specific code section. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely changes the text of an existing law.
qwen_block.s: Section 10751 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking out “(other than transportation by rail)” in subsections (a) and (b).

opus.w: This is a technical amendment. It removes a rail exclusion from section 10751 and says which expenses the amended section covers, including ones incurred before the effective date. It creates no comment period, rulemaking authority, hearing, advisory committee, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The mention of penalties under section 10761 is about enforcement, not outside parties taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: Section 10751 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking out “(other than transportation by rail)” in subsections (a) and (b).
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section amends a transportation statute that the Interstate Commerce Commission enforced, and it mentions penalties. That might suggest a regulatory process with outside input. But the text only strikes a rail exclusion ("(other than transportation by rail)") and makes the change apply to past and future expenses. It sets up no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute regarding the applicability of certain provisions to rail transportation. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation with outside parties, public hearings, comment periods, or advisory committees. The text merely changes the scope of an existing legal provision without introducing any participatory mechanisms.
qwen_chat.s: Section 10751 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking out “(other than transportation by rail)” in subsections (a) and (b).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that removing the exclusion of rail transportation implies a change in regulatory scope that could involve public comment or consultation. However, the text itself is purely a technical amendment to a statute's applicability and contains no procedural requirements for public input, hearings, or consultation with outside parties. It does not grant rights to sue, nor does it establish advisory bodies or comment periods.
